margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Targets are non-GAAP operating margin; street fields below use consensus operating_income for the gap and consensus EBITDA for the margin path.

statements.quote: Operating profit of $924 million to $932 million, up approximately 21% year-over-year, and equating to an operating margin of approximately 23.7%.

street.gap_assumption: Compares the FY2027 non-GAAP operating margin guide (~23.7%) with consensus FY2027 operating_income / revenue (929.4M / 3,929.6M = 23.65%), same metric. FY2026 in the EBITDA row is reported (FYE July 2026). The legacy 20% to 22% long-term range sits below every consensus year.

evidence_of_progress.note: Order is [Q3 FY2026 (Apr-2026), Q4 FY2026 (Jul-2026)], EBITDA margin YoY from consensus actuals (Q4 derived as FY2026 minus Q1 to Q3). CFO-stated non-GAAP operating margin: Q4 FY2026 24.3%, up 220 bps YoY; FY2026 22.9%, up 120 bps (doc 217612). Margin is already above the old long-term range; FY2027 guide adds about 80 bps.

disqualifier_reason: Margin target already reflected in consensus: FY2027 consensus operating margin 23.65% vs the CFO's ~23.7% guide (5 bps gap), and the only long-term range (20% to 22%) was surpassed in FY2026 at 22.9%. Not a low-margin business (27.3% LTM EBITDA margin), so there is no GXO-style margin gap to close.
verdict: Not a GXO setup: cheap and de-rated with an external CFO, but a high-margin software name whose only numeric margin framing is a one-year guide the street already models; the 2026-10-06 Investor Day is the only thing that could create a gap.
open_questions: Will the 2026-10-06 Investor Day replace the stale 20% to 22% long-term range with a new operating or FCF margin target, and is it above the 23.65% FY2027 consensus?
How much of the FY2027 FCF margin step-down (23% to 23.5% guide) is memory and component CapEx that reverses?
Does the 3% workforce restructuring ($30M to $33M charges) fund AI reinvestment or drop to margin?
